source.title: SafeRedir: Prompt Embedding Redirection for Robust Unlearning in Image Generation Models
source.authors: Renyang Liu; Kangjie Chen; Han Qiu; Jie Zhang; Kwok-Yan Lam; Tian-Wei Zhang; See-kiong Ng

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. PDF extraction introduces some garbling, especially in figures and flattened tables.
record.tranche_reason: Tests prompt-based reactivation and a defensive unlearning method in image-generation models, extending the unlearning and attack question to a different modality from the LLM-focused claim.
record.gate_note: The paper directly evaluates unlearned image-generation models under paraphrased, jailbreak-crafted, and adversarial prompts, reporting attack success rates. It also reports forgetting and preservation measures for SafeRedir. Cited findings about other work are not recorded as rows. The separately reported UnlearnDiffAtk results for every baseline, and many additional ablation results, are omitted under the row limit.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether three kinds of prompt reactivate concepts erased from Stable Diffusion v1.4 by ten unlearning baselines: human-written paraphrases (I2P), jailbreak prompts (MMA) and optimized adversarial prompts (UnlearnDiffAtk). It does this in its own empirical study (Sec. 3.3, Observation 3) and in Tables 7-8. It also tests its own inference-time counter-method, SafeRedir, against the same attacks and against an adaptive attack. That makes it version E, and the attack part of A, in a new setting: text-to-image diffusion rather than LLMs. It also bears on F, through SafeRedir and the robustness-oriented baselines (AdvUnlearn, Receler, RECE). The results carry over to the LLM-knowledge claim only by analogy.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SafeRedir balances forgetting, robustness to paraphrased and adversarial prompts, semantic preservation and visual fidelity. They limit this to the evaluated Stable Diffusion-compatible models. Their Sec. 3 study also concludes that existing erasure methods forget incompletely and that prompt variants reactivate erased concepts.
record.recipe_differences: This is an inference-time prompt-embedding redirection wrapper for image-generation models, not an LLM unlearning or weight-removal recipe. It does not modify the diffusion backbone; the redirector itself is trained on aligned safe–unsafe prompt pairs.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack outcomes vary by prompt dataset and unlearning task. SafeRedir's UnlearnDiffAtk ASR is 9.38% on NSFW, 50.16% on Van Gogh, and 3.12% on Church; its adaptive NSFW attack sweep ranges from 1.56% to 7.81%.
record.problems: Forgetting is assessed with detector-based FSR rather than a stated chance-level accuracy baseline. The paper reports no error bars or confidence intervals for these results. The stated scope is evaluated Stable Diffusion-compatible image-generation models, not LLMs.
record.rows_left_out: Table 8 reports ASR and attack time for other unlearned methods across NSFW, Van Gogh, and Church; only SafeRedir's three task-specific ASRs are retained here because of the row limit. Table 5 baseline FSR results beyond SafeRedir, Table 6 other methods' preservation results, and Table 10–11 integration results are also omitted. The paper reports many additional ablations in Table 12–14; these concern SafeRedir's internal design or sampling setup rather than the listed recovery attacks.

untested.parts: No LLMs and no accuracy-versus-chance measure; forgetting is detector-based FSR. The rows cover only whether prompt attacks recover the concept. No fine-tuning, ablation or quantization attacks.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of deletion versus blocking. SafeRedir by design leaves the concept in the weights, but this is not tested as an attack.

No LLMs. Prompts are only I2P paraphrases, MMA jailbreaks and UnlearnDiffAtk on SD v1.4; there are no other-language or in-context attacks. No original-model ASR on the I2P/MMA prompts is reported, so recovery is judged against explicit-prompt residuals.
SafeRedir and the robust baselines face only black-box and prompt-based attacks. There are no fine-tuning, internal-edit or quantization attacks, no white-box removal of the wrapper, and no LLMs.

missing.what: Embedding Sanitizer (ES) baseline ASR: I2P 6.57 and MMA 15.83, against an explicit-prompt residual of 4.91 (FSR 95.09). This is no recovery on I2P and partial recovery on MMA. It also bears on A. It is not recorded and not declared in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) Version ids. The merge refused the earlier verdict because the record uses V1-V6. By content: V1 (unlearning works) is A, V5 (prompting) is E and V6 (counter-methods) is F. Every row r1-r33 has one row_fixes item with declared ids or none.
(2) Relation and tranche changed from discusses/T6 to tests/T3. The earlier test_reason said the study mainly reports its own wrapper. The text contradicts this: Sec. 3 is an empirical study of existing erasure methods, and Tables 7-8 report the baselines' reactivation under prompt attacks. The catalog also treats diffusion concept-erasure attack studies as T3 new-setting tests of E and F (e.g. the repaired verdicts for arXiv:2604.09391 and arXiv:2504.21307, and a similar pruning study in verdicts.json). The earlier note itself sketched this alternative.
(3) Row links. r8-r27 go to A and E. AdvUnlearn, RECE and Receler, which the text describes as robustness-oriented, also go to F. r28-r33 (SafeRedir, which leaves weights unchanged) go to F only. r1-r7 stay none as own-method, no-attack performance.
(4) The two earlier fits_no_version entries are dropped because their rows are now linked. The ES missing entry now names E rather than 'none'.

State convention: for r8-r33 the state is recovery of the erased concept, judged against each method's explicit-prompt residual (100 minus Table 5 FSR). For A and F, recovery means the claim fails. This reference is approximate. I2P, MMA and UnlearnDiffAtk use other prompts and perhaps other detectors. The paper reports no ASR for the original SD on I2P or MMA.

Results left out of the rows but declared in rows_left_out:
- Table 8 (UnlearnDiffAtk on baselines) would strengthen E. ESD reaches 56.25 on NSFW and ConceptPrune 100/100/96.88, and every baseline is at or above 53 on Van Gogh, including AdvUnlearn (53.12), so AdvUnlearn's F support holds only for I2P/MMA.
- Table 10: after SafeRedir is added, Van Gogh ASR is still 40.62-60.16.
- Table 6: AdvUnlearn and MACE have the highest NSFW CSDR (12.03, 12.76), a preservation cost relevant to A's 'keeps general ability'.

Other points:
- The threat model is black-box only. SafeRedir is an external wrapper that leaves the concept in the weights.
- As extracted, Fig. 12 at delta=0 reads 3.12, while Table 8 gives 9.38 for the same attack.
- No uncertainty estimates are reported.
- No instructions to the reader were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The paper evaluates image-generation models, not LLMs; its forgetting measure is detector-based FSR rather than targeted-knowledge accuracy against a chance baseline. General ability is assessed through image-preservation measures, not broad task capability.
No small unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact fine-tuning set is used to recover knowledge.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether an internal edit deletes knowledge versus blocking access.
No low-bit quantization of unlearned weights.
Tests paraphrased and adversarial prompt attacks in image-generation models; does not test other languages or recovery through in-context information.
Tests SafeRedir against the prompt-based attacks evaluated in the paper; does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation ablation, or quantization attacks.

rows.stage_stated: inference-time wrapper applied to Stable Diffusion v1.4
rows.operation_detail: Evaluates forgetting on the NSFW task using mean FSR across responding detectors.
rows.note: FSR is defined as the proportion of generated images in which sensitive content is not detected; it is not an accuracy measure with a stated chance baseline.
rows.check: SafeRedir's own forgetting on explicit NSFW prompts (Table 5 FSR 99.84), with no attack. This is own-method performance and bears on no version. It supplies the no-attack residual (0.16%) used as the reference for F rows r28-r30 and r33.
